answer: A reputation system can cap an agent’s influence until it completes tasks verified by independent counterparties, with payment held in escrow. New identities cannot gain trust through self-endorsements, and each must pay for real work and build its own record. A sybil attacker therefore faces a growing cost for every account, while the cap limits damage from untrusted agents. In an orchard market, even lotus accounts must earn trust over a long horizon.
